bengal-famine-of-1943.name: Bengal famine of 1943
bengal-famine-of-1943.summary: A World War II-era famine in British India's Bengal and Orissa provinces that killed an estimated 800,000 to 3.8 million people from starvation and disease.

indian-chinese-cuisine.name: Indian Chinese cuisine
indian-chinese-cuisine.summary: A style of Chinese cooking adapted to Indian tastes, begun by Chinese immigrants in British-ruled India such as Calcutta, blending Indian spices with Chinese sauces and techniques.

japanese-occupation-of-burma.name: Japanese occupation of Burma
japanese-occupation-of-burma.summary: 1942–1945 Japanese occupation of Burma during World War II, initially backed by Burmese nationalists seeking independence from Britain but later resented, and blamed for 170,000 to 250,000 civilian deaths.

green-revolution.name: Green Revolution
green-revolution.summary: A wave of new farming technology, including high-yield dwarf wheat and rice, chemical fertilizers and controlled irrigation, that greatly raised crop yields worldwide; leader Norman Borlaug won the 1970 Nobel Peace Prize.

madrasi-para.name: Madrasi Para
madrasi-para.summary: Neighborhood in Karachi settled mostly by Tamil Hindu migrants in the early 20th century, known for preserving South Indian food traditions such as dosa.

mughlai-cuisine.name: Mughlai cuisine
mughlai-cuisine.summary: A style of cooking developed in the Indo-Persian courts of the Mughal Empire, blending Persian methods like the tandoor with the spices and vegetables of the Indian subcontinent.

winston-churchill.name: Winston Churchill
winston-churchill.summary: British statesman and Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1940 to 1945 and 1951 to 1955, who led Britain through the Second World War.

manchurian-dish.name: Manchurian (dish)
manchurian-dish.summary: An Indian Chinese dish of deep-fried chicken, cauliflower or other ingredients in a soy-based sauce, invented in 1975 by Nelson Wang despite its name and bearing little resemblance to actual Manchu or Chinese cuisine.

nelson-wang.name: Nelson Wang
nelson-wang.summary: An Indian restaurateur of Chinese descent, founder of Mumbai's China Garden restaurant, credited by various sources with inventing the dish Chicken Manchurian.

ladakh.name: Ladakh
ladakh.summary: A high-altitude region of the wider Kashmir area, now a union territory of India, historically important as a crossroads of trade routes.

butter-tea.name: Gurgur cha
butter-tea.summary: A Ladakhi name for butter tea, made from strong green tea, butter, and salt churned together, named for the sound the churn makes.

national-gallery-of-modern-art.name: National Gallery of Modern Art
national-gallery-of-modern-art.summary: India's premier modern art gallery, established in 1954 in New Delhi with branches in Mumbai and Bangalore, holding over 17,000 works by more than 2,000 artists.

india-art-fair.name: India Art Fair
india-art-fair.summary: India's largest annual contemporary art fair, held in New Delhi since 2008 and among the world's most attended art fairs.

indian-institute-of-architects.name: Indian Institute of Architects
indian-institute-of-architects.summary: A learned society of architects established in 1917, headquartered in Mumbai and a member of several international architecture bodies.

all-india-fine-arts-and-crafts-society.name: AIFACS
all-india-fine-arts-and-crafts-society.summary: Independent Indian arts organisation founded in Delhi in 1928, which organises exhibitions and prestigious art awards and once fed into India's national arts academies.
all-india-fine-arts-and-crafts-society.source_title: All India Fine Arts and Crafts Society

sarada-ukil.name: Sarada Ukil
sarada-ukil.summary: Bengali actor and artist (1888–1940) known for a role in the film Prem Sanyas / The Light of Asia, and father of art pioneer Shantanu Ukil.

abanindranath-tagore.name: Abanindranath Tagore
abanindranath-tagore.summary: Indian painter (1871-1951) who founded the Bengal school of art, led the Indian Society of Oriental Art from 1907, and was also known as a children's writer.

louis-kahn.name: Louis Kahn
louis-kahn.summary: An Estonian-born American architect (1901–1974) known for monumental, monolithic buildings, who taught at Yale and the University of Pennsylvania.

achyut-kanvinde.name: Achyut Kanvinde
achyut-kanvinde.summary: Indian architect (1916–2002) known for functionalist and Brutalist work, including IIT Kanpur; awarded the Padma Shri in 1974.

b-v-doshi.name: B. V. Doshi
b-v-doshi.summary: An Indian architect (1927–2023) who worked under Le Corbusier and Louis Kahn and pioneered modernist and brutalist architecture in India, becoming the first Indian to win the Pritzker Prize in 2018.

fariborz-sahba.name: Fariborz Sahba
fariborz-sahba.summary: Iranian-American architect, born 1948, best known for designing the Baháʼí Lotus Temple in New Delhi, India.

charles-correa.name: Charles Correa
charles-correa.summary: Indian architect and urban planner (1930-2015) based in Mumbai, credited with shaping modern architecture in post-independence India.

haider-ali-artist.name: Haider Ali
haider-ali-artist.summary: A Pakistani painter renowned for truck art, who gained international attention in 2002 after painting the first authentic Pakistani truck in North America for the Smithsonian.

smithsonian-folklife-festival.name: Smithsonian Folklife Festival
smithsonian-folklife-festival.summary: An annual two-week cultural exhibition on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., held since 1967 and featuring performers and craftspeople from around the world.

bylakuppe.name: Bylakuppe
bylakuppe.summary: A region in the Indian state of Karnataka home to Tibetan refugee settlements founded in 1961 and 1969, with several major Tibetan Buddhist monasteries.

vidhana-soudha.name: Vidhana Soudha
vidhana-soudha.summary: A Neo-Dravidian style building in Bangalore, completed in 1956, that houses Karnataka's state legislature.

stella-kramrisch.name: Stella Kramrisch
stella-kramrisch.summary: An Austrian-American art historian and curator (1896–1993) considered the leading specialist on Indian art for most of the 20th century, teaching in India, Europe and the United States.

nandalal-bose.name: Nandalal Bose
nandalal-bose.summary: Pioneering modern Indian painter (1882–1966) known for an 'Indian style' influenced by the Ajanta murals, later invited to illustrate the Constitution of India.

jamini-roy.name: Jamini Roy
jamini-roy.summary: Indian painter (1887–1972) honored with the Padma Bhushan in 1954, known for a simplified style inspired by traditional bazaar temple paintings.

niharranjan-ray.name: Niharranjan Ray
niharranjan-ray.summary: Indian Bengali historian (1903–1981) known for his works on art history and Indian history.

b-c-sanyal.name: B. C. Sanyal
b-c-sanyal.summary: An Indian painter, sculptor and art teacher (1902–2003) seen as a founding figure of Indian modernism, awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1984.

nazar-amulet.name: Nazar (amulet)
nazar-amulet.summary: An eye-shaped amulet believed to ward off the evil eye, known by many names across Middle Eastern, South Asian, and Mediterranean cultures.

indian-national-army.name: Indian National Army
indian-national-army.summary: A Japanese-allied force of Indian nationalists led by Subhas Chandra Bose in World War II, made largely of captured British Indian Army soldiers and aiming to end British rule in India.

battle-of-kohima.name: Battle of Kohima
battle-of-kohima.summary: Turning-point 1944 battle around this town in Northeast India that halted Japan's invasion of British India; sometimes called the 'Stalingrad of the East'.

battle-of-imphal.name: Battle of Imphal
battle-of-imphal.summary: A 1944 World War II battle around the Indian city of Imphal in which Allied forces repelled a Japanese invasion attempt, a turning point of the Burma campaign.

waziristan.name: Waziristan
waziristan.summary: A mountainous region of Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, split into North and South Waziristan districts.

hari-singh.name: Hari Singh
hari-singh.summary: Last ruling Maharaja of the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir (1923–1952) of the Dogra dynasty, who acceded to India in 1947 to secure military help against invasion.

instrument-of-accession.name: Instrument of Accession
instrument-of-accession.summary: A legal document created under a 1935 British law that in 1947 let rulers of India's princely states join either the new dominion of India or Pakistan after partition.

srinagar.name: Srinagar
srinagar.summary: The largest city and summer capital of Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir, in the Kashmir Valley on the Jhelum River, founded in the 6th century as a center of learning and handicrafts.

a-a-k-niazi.name: A. A. K. Niazi
a-a-k-niazi.summary: Pakistani general who commanded the Eastern Command during the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War and surrendered to Indian forces at Dhaka on 16 December 1971, ending the war.

north-east-frontier-agency.name: North-East Frontier Agency
north-east-frontier-agency.summary: Political division of British India and later India, administered from Shillong; reorganised from earlier frontier tracts in 1954 and replaced by Arunachal Pradesh in 1972.

aksai-chin.name: Aksai Chin
aksai-chin.summary: A region administered by China as part of Xinjiang and Tibet, forming the easternmost part of Kashmir and disputed with India since 1959.

ardagh-johnson-line.name: Johnson Line
ardagh-johnson-line.summary: A boundary line for Kashmir's northeastern frontier drawn by surveyor William Johnson and recommended by John Charles Ardagh, recognised by India but not by China in the Aksai Chin dispute.

mcmahon-line.name: McMahon Line
mcmahon-line.summary: The 1914 boundary between British India and Tibet set at the Simla Convention, still forming the de facto China-India border today, though its legal status remains disputed by China.

operation-meghdoot.name: Operation Meghdoot
operation-meghdoot.summary: 1984 Indian military operation that seized most of the Siachen Glacier in the Himalayas, preempting a planned Pakistani move and starting the ongoing high-altitude Siachen conflict.

siachen-glacier.name: Siachen Glacier
siachen-glacier.summary: 76-kilometre glacier in the Karakoram range of the Himalayas, the longest in the Karakoram, disputed between India and Pakistan and under Indian administration since 1984.

saltoro-mountains.name: Saltoro Ridge
saltoro-mountains.summary: The main ridge of the Saltoro Mountains, part of the Karakoram Range, running along the southwest side of the Siachen Glacier and today straddling the disputed India-Pakistan front line.

sia-la.name: Sia La
sia-la.summary: Mountain pass on the Saltoro Ridge, under Indian control, that connects the Siachen Glacier to the Pakistani-held Kondus Glacier and valley.

bilafond-la.name: Bilafond La
bilafond-la.summary: A mountain pass on the Saltoro Ridge near the Siachen Glacier, on the ancient Silk Road between the Indian subcontinent and China; India has held it since capturing it in 1984 during the Siachen Conflict.

india-gate.name: India Gate
india-gate.summary: A war memorial in New Delhi honouring over 74,000 Indian Army soldiers who died between 1914 and 1921, designed by Edwin Lutyens in the style of Roman triumphal arches.

edwin-lutyens.name: Edwin Lutyens
edwin-lutyens.summary: English architect (1869–1944) known for country houses and war memorials, and for his major role designing New Delhi, including the India Gate.

third-anglo-afghan-war.name: Third Anglo-Afghan War
third-anglo-afghan-war.summary: A short 1919 war in which Emir Amanullah Khan invaded British India seeking full Afghan independence; it ended with a treaty restoring Afghan control of foreign affairs.

operation-chengiz-khan.name: Operation Chengiz Khan
operation-chengiz-khan.summary: Pakistan Air Force's preemptive strikes on Indian airbases and radar sites on 3 December 1971, opening the Indo-Pakistani War of 1971; named after Genghis Khan, it caused little damage but led India to declare war.

amar-jawan-jyoti.name: Amar Jawan Jyoti
amar-jawan-jyoti.summary: India's war memorial flame at India Gate, built after the 1971 war and inaugurated in 1972 by Indira Gandhi; it served as India's Tomb of the Unknown Soldier until merged with a newer memorial in 2022.

indira-gandhi.name: Indira Gandhi
indira-gandhi.summary: Indian stateswoman who served as prime minister from 1966 to 1977 and again from 1980 to 1984, the country's first and only female prime minister, assassinated in 1984. She was the daughter of India's first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.

renya-mutaguchi.name: Renya Mutaguchi
renya-mutaguchi.summary: A Japanese army officer (1888–1966) who served in World War II as the field commander of Japanese forces at the Battle of Imphal.

orde-wingate.name: Orde Wingate
orde-wingate.summary: British Army officer, 1903 to 1944, known for unconventional tactics, who set up a counter-insurgency unit in Mandatory Palestine and later led the Chindit missions against Japanese forces in Burma.

chindits.name: Chindits
chindits.summary: British and Indian special forces units formed by Orde Wingate for long-range raids behind Japanese lines in Burma during World War II, known for grueling marches and heavy losses to disease.

indian-ocean-raid.name: Indian Ocean raid
indian-ocean-raid.summary: A Japanese naval sortie from 31 March to 10 April 1942 that struck Allied shipping and bases around British Ceylon but failed to find most of the British Eastern Fleet.

british-ceylon.name: Ceylon
british-ceylon.summary: Former name for the island of present-day Sri Lanka, under British imperial rule from 1815 until independence in 1948.

kilindini-harbour.name: Kilindini Harbour
kilindini-harbour.summary: A natural deep-water inlet at Mombasa, Kenya, forming the main part of the Port of Mombasa, the largest port in East Africa.

sahitya-akademi.name: Sahitya Akademi
sahitya-akademi.summary: India's National Academy of Letters, founded in 1954 to promote literature across India's languages; it runs workshops, gives research grants, and presents annual literary awards.

eighth-schedule-to-the-constitution-of-i.name: Eighth Schedule
eighth-schedule-to-the-constitution-of-i.summary: The section of India's Constitution listing officially recognized languages, currently numbering 22.
eighth-schedule-to-the-constitution-of-i.source_title: Eighth Schedule to the Constitution of India

ghadar-di-gunj.name: Ghadar di Gunj
ghadar-di-gunj.summary: Collection of nationalist and socialist songs and poems published in 1913–14 by the Ghadar movement's press in San Francisco, later banned by British India as seditious.

gurmukhi.name: Gurmukhi
gurmukhi.summary: A writing system developed from the Landa scripts, popularly credited to the second Sikh guru, Guru Angad, and used to write the Punjabi language and Sikh scripture.

shahmukhi.name: Shahmukhi
shahmukhi.summary: A right-to-left script derived from the Perso-Arabic alphabet, used for writing Punjabi mainly in Pakistan, as opposed to the Gurmukhi script used in India.

nissim-ezekiel.name: Nissim Ezekiel
nissim-ezekiel.summary: Indian poet, actor, playwright and critic (1924-2004), a foundational figure in Indian English poetry, awarded the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1983.

a-k-ramanujan.name: A. K. Ramanujan
a-k-ramanujan.summary: Indian poet, scholar and translator (1929-1993) who studied literature and linguistics across five languages and won the Sahitya Akademi Award posthumously in 1999.

r-parthasarathy.name: R. Parthasarathy
r-parthasarathy.summary: Indian poet, translator, critic and editor (1934–2026).

kamala-surayya.name: Kamala Das
kamala-surayya.summary: Indian poet and author (1934–2009), writing in English as Kamala Das and in Malayalam as Madhavikutty, known for candid depictions of female sexuality and her autobiography.

arun-kolatkar.name: Arun Kolatkar
arun-kolatkar.summary: Indian poet (1932–2004) who wrote in Marathi and English; his collection Jejuri won the Commonwealth Poetry Prize in 1977.

khamba-thoibi-sheireng.name: Khamba Thoibi Sheireng
khamba-thoibi-sheireng.summary: A Meitei-language epic poem of about 39,000 verses composed by Hijam Anganghal, based on the love story of prince Khamba and princess Thoibi. Considered the national epic of Manipur and the third-longest Indian epic.

khamba-and-thoibi.name: Khamba and Thoibi
khamba-and-thoibi.summary: An ancient Meitei legend from the Moirang kingdom, called the 'national romantic legend of Manipur.' It inspired the epic poem Khamba Thoibi Sheireng and was later translated into Assamese as a classic tale.

muhammad-iqbal.name: Muhammad Iqbal
muhammad-iqbal.summary: Islamic philosopher and poet (1877–1938) whose Urdu poetry is among the most celebrated of the 20th century and whose vision helped inspire the Pakistan Movement.

the-call-of-the-marching-bell.name: Bang-e-Dara
the-call-of-the-marching-bell.summary: The first Urdu philosophical poetry collection by Muhammad Iqbal, published in 1924, written across three phases of his life.
the-call-of-the-marching-bell.source_title: The Call of the Marching Bell

sare-jahan-se-accha.name: Tarana-e-Hindi
sare-jahan-se-accha.summary: An Urdu patriotic poem for children written by Muhammad Iqbal in 1904, later published as 'Sare Jahan se Accha,' that became an anthem of opposition to British rule.

cilappatikaram.name: Cilappatikaram
cilappatikaram.summary: An ancient Tamil epic poem of 5,730 lines, probably composed in the 5th century CE, telling the tragic love story of Kannaki and her husband Kōvalan.

sahitya-akademi-translation-prize.name: Sahitya Akademi Translation Prize
sahitya-akademi-translation-prize.summary: A literary award established in 1989 by India's Sahitya Akademi, honoring outstanding translations in 24 major Indian languages, with a plaque and cash prize.

pandey-bechan-sharma.name: Pandey Bechan Sharma
pandey-bechan-sharma.summary: Indian writer (1900-1967), known by the pen name Ugra, noted for provocative satirical journalism, fiction and autobiography.

banarsidas-chaturvedi.name: Banarsidas Chaturvedi
banarsidas-chaturvedi.summary: A Hindi-language writer and journalist (1892–1985) awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1973, whose work explored nationalism, social reform and the experiences of Indians overseas.

firaq-gorakhpuri.name: Firaq Gorakhpuri
firaq-gorakhpuri.summary: Indian Urdu poet, writer and critic (1896–1982), born Raghupati Sahay, regarded as one of the most noted contemporary Urdu poets from India.

ghazal.name: Ghazal
ghazal.summary: Poetic form originating in 7th-century Arabic poetry that deals with love and loss, later flourishing in Persian poetry and spreading across South Asia and Turkey.

dom-moraes.name: Dom Moraes
dom-moraes.summary: Indian writer and poet (1938 to 2004) who published nearly 30 books in English and is seen as a foundational figure in Indian English literature.

jawaharlal-nehru.name: Jawaharlal Nehru
jawaharlal-nehru.summary: India's first prime minister after 1947 independence, serving nearly 17 years and promoting parliamentary democracy, secularism and science, having earlier led the Indian nationalist movement.

indian-institutes-of-technology.name: Indian Institutes of Technology
indian-institutes-of-technology.summary: A network of 23 autonomous public engineering and technology universities in India, established in 1950 and designated Institutions of National Importance.

kharagpur.name: Kharagpur
kharagpur.summary: An industrial city in West Bengal, India, home to IIT Kharagpur, the oldest and largest Indian Institute of Technology.

isro.name: ISRO
isro.summary: India's national space agency, headquartered in Bengaluru, responsible for satellites, space exploration and lunar and Mars missions since its founding in 1962.

pokhran.name: Pokhran
pokhran.summary: A desert town in Rajasthan, India, near the site of the country's first underground nuclear weapon test in 1974.

all-india-institute-of-medical-sciences-.name: AIIMS Delhi
all-india-institute-of-medical-sciences-.summary: Public medical university and hospital in New Delhi established under a 1956 Act, regarded as among India's best medical research institutions.
all-india-institute-of-medical-sciences-.source_title: All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Delhi

national-institutional-ranking-framework.name: National Institutional Ranking Framework
national-institutional-ranking-framework.summary: An annual ranking system launched in 2015 by India's Ministry of Education to rank institutions of higher education across categories like engineering and medicine.

pakistan-institute-of-nuclear-science-te.name: PINSTECH
pakistan-institute-of-nuclear-science-te.summary: A federally funded Pakistani research complex near Islamabad, designed by American architect Edward Durell Stone and completed in 1965, briefly repurposed for weapons work before returning to civilian science.
pakistan-institute-of-nuclear-science-te.source_title: Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science & Technology

nilore.name: Nilore
nilore.summary: A town near Islamabad, Pakistan, home to the Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science & Technology, where key nuclear research has taken place since the 1960s.

edward-durell-stone.name: Edward Durell Stone
edward-durell-stone.summary: An American architect (1902-1978) known for formal, highly decorative buildings of the 1950s and 60s, including the Museum of Modern Art and the Kennedy Center.

maulana-azad.name: Maulana Azad
maulana-azad.summary: Indian independence activist and writer (1888–1958) who led the Khilafat Movement, became a senior Congress leader, and served as India's first education minister.

national-institutes-of-technology.name: National Institutes of Technology
national-institutes-of-technology.summary: A group of centrally funded Indian technical institutes, originally established as Regional Engineering Colleges, now recognized under a 2007 act as institutions of national importance.

nature-index.name: Nature Index
nature-index.summary: A database launched in 2014 that tracks scientific output of institutions and countries by counting articles in leading journals, producing annual rankings including of fast-rising universities.

abdus-salam.name: Abdus Salam
abdus-salam.summary: Pakistani theoretical physicist and Nobel laureate (1926–1996), the first Pakistani and second person from a Muslim country to win a Nobel Prize, for work unifying the weak and electromagnetic forces.

atoms-for-peace.name: Atoms for Peace
atoms-for-peace.summary: 1953 speech and program launched by US president Eisenhower to share nuclear equipment and knowledge for peaceful purposes with schools, hospitals and research institutions worldwide.

ballabhgarh.name: Ballabhgarh
ballabhgarh.summary: A town near Faridabad in Haryana, India, founded in 1739 by Raja Balram Singh; its last king, Nahar Singh, was executed in 1858 for joining the 1857 uprising.

rockefeller-foundation.name: Rockefeller Foundation
rockefeller-foundation.summary: American philanthropic foundation created by John D. Rockefeller and his son in 1913, one of the world's largest, whose work influenced institutions like the World Health Organization.

india-pakistan-war-of-1971.name: India–Pakistan war of 1971
india-pakistan-war-of-1971.summary: A December 1971 war between India and Pakistan during the Bangladesh Liberation War, ending in Pakistan's surrender in Dhaka and the creation of Bangladesh.

zirconium-alloys.name: Zircaloy
zirconium-alloys.summary: A trademarked family of zirconium alloys used mainly as cladding for nuclear fuel rods, valued for low neutron absorption, corrosion resistance and hardness.

kundian-nuclear-fuel-complex.name: Kundian Nuclear Fuel Complex
kundian-nuclear-fuel-complex.summary: Nuclear fuel manufacturing plant in Kundian, Punjab, Pakistan, owned by the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission, producing uranium oxide fuel and reactor components for the country's power plants.

british-raj.name: British Raj
british-raj.summary: Period of direct rule by the British Crown over the Indian subcontinent, from 1858 until 1947, when it was partitioned into India and Pakistan.

dominion-of-india.name: Union of India
dominion-of-india.summary: Independent dominion within the British Commonwealth from 1947 to 1950, formed after the partition of British India, and the immediate predecessor of the Republic of India.

dominion-of-pakistan.name: Dominion of Pakistan
dominion-of-pakistan.summary: Pakistani state from 1947 to 1956 as an independent federal dominion in the British Commonwealth, created under the Indian Independence Act 1947, before becoming a republic.

indian-national-congress.name: Indian National Congress
indian-national-congress.summary: India's oldest political party, founded in 1885, which led the Indian independence movement under Mahatma Gandhi and later dominated politics under Jawaharlal Nehru.

quit-india-movement.name: Quit India Movement
quit-india-movement.summary: A 1942 campaign launched by Mahatma Gandhi demanding an end to British rule in India during World War II, which led to the mass imprisonment of Congress leaders.

all-india-muslim-league.name: All-India Muslim League
all-india-muslim-league.summary: Political party in British India, active from 1906 to 1947, that advocated for Muslim interests and led the movement to create Pakistan.

hindu-mahasabha.name: Hindu Mahasabha
hindu-mahasabha.summary: A far-right Hindu nationalist Indian political party founded in 1915, whose member Nathuram Godse assassinated Mahatma Gandhi.

forty-second-amendment-of-the-constituti.name: Forty-second Amendment
forty-second-amendment-of-the-constituti.summary: A sweeping 1976 amendment to India's constitution, passed under Indira Gandhi's Emergency, that curbed court powers and expanded central government authority.
forty-second-amendment-of-the-constituti.source_title: Forty-second Amendment of the Constitution of India

s-r-bommai-v-union-of-india.name: S. R. Bommai v. Union of India
s-r-bommai-v-union-of-india.summary: A landmark 1994 Indian Supreme Court ruling that curbed misuse of Article 356, which had let the president impose direct rule over state governments.
s-r-bommai-v-union-of-india.source_title: S. R. Bommai v. Union of India

victor-hope-2nd-marquess-of-linlithgow.name: Marquess of Linlithgow
victor-hope-2nd-marquess-of-linlithgow.summary: British colonial administrator who served as Governor-General and Viceroy of India from 1936 to 1943, and also as Chancellor of the University of Edinburgh.

royal-indian-navy.name: Royal Indian Navy
royal-indian-navy.summary: The naval force of British India, evolving since 1612 from the East India Company's Marine through several renamings before becoming the Royal Indian Navy in 1934.

frederick-pethick-lawrence-1st-baron-pet.name: Lord Pethick-Lawrence
frederick-pethick-lawrence-1st-baron-pet.summary: British Labour politician (1871-1961) who campaigned for women's suffrage.

stafford-cripps.name: Stafford Cripps
stafford-cripps.summary: British Labour politician (1889–1952) who served as ambassador to the USSR during World War II and later led a 1942 mission to negotiate with Indian leaders over wartime cooperation.

hindu-marriage-act-1955.name: Hindu Marriage Act
hindu-marriage-act-1955.summary: A 1955 Indian law regulating Hindu marriage, one of several Hindu Code Bills enacted around that time in India.

subhas-chandra-bose.name: Subhas Chandra Bose
subhas-chandra-bose.summary: Indian anti-colonial nationalist (1897–1945) hailed by many Indians for defying British rule, though his wartime alliances with Nazi Germany and Japan left a controversial legacy.

andaman-and-nicobar-islands.name: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
andaman-and-nicobar-islands.summary: A union territory of India made up of 836 islands in the Bay of Bengal, only 31 of them inhabited, with Port Blair as its capital.

azad-hind.name: Azad Hind
azad-hind.summary: A Japanese-backed provisional Indian government set up in Singapore in 1943 under Subhas Chandra Bose, aiming to end British rule with Axis support.

kohima.name: Kohima
kohima.summary: The capital of Nagaland in northeast India, originally an Angami Naga village that became a British administrative headquarters in 1878 and the site of a major World War II battle in 1944.

krushna-chandra-gajapati.name: Krushna Chandra Gajapati
krushna-chandra-gajapati.summary: Key figure in creating the Indian state of Odisha, a scion of the Paralakhemundi estate and owner of the Delanga estate, from the Eastern Ganga Dynasty; he became Odisha's first Prime Minister, and Gajapati District is named after him.

paralakhemundi.name: Paralakhemundi
paralakhemundi.summary: A historic town in the Indian state of Odisha that later became capital of the Paralakhemundi Estate under the Eastern Ganga dynasty, and is a longstanding cultural center of the region.

shiromani-akali-dal.name: Shiromani Akali Dal
shiromani-akali-dal.summary: A Sikh-centric political party in Punjab, India, founded in 1920, the second-oldest party in the country after Congress.

rashtriya-swayamsevak-sangh.name: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh
rashtriya-swayamsevak-sangh.summary: Indian Hindu nationalist volunteer organisation founded in 1925, the progenitor of the Sangh Parivar family of groups that includes the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party.

manikya-dynasty.name: Manikya dynasty
manikya-dynasty.summary: The ruling house of the Twipra Kingdom, later Tripura State, in northeast India from the early 15th century until it joined India in 1949.

bir-bikram-kishore-manikya-bahadur.name: Bir Bikram Kishore
bir-bikram-kishore-manikya-bahadur.summary: A king of Tripura State who lived from 1908 to 1947, known as 'the architect of modern Tripura'.

kanchan-prava-devi.name: Kanchan Prava Devi
kanchan-prava-devi.summary: Queen of Tripura by marriage to its king Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya Bahadur; after his 1947 death she served as regent until Tripura merged with India in 1949.

kirit-bikram-kishore-deb-barman.name: Kirit Bikram Kishore
kirit-bikram-kishore-deb-barman.summary: The 185th and last King of Tripura, a princely state in northeastern India, who lived from 1933 to 2006; his formal coronation in 1941 never gave him real royal power.

porbandar-state.name: Porbandar
porbandar-state.summary: A princely state on India's coast during the British Raj, ruled by the Jethwa dynasty; its last ruler acceded to independent India in 1947.

jethwa-dynasty.name: Jethwa dynasty
jethwa-dynasty.summary: A Rajput dynasty that ruled the Porbandar region of Gujarat, India, from the 7th century until India's independence in 1947.

natwarsinhji-bhavsinhji.name: Rana Natwarsinhji
natwarsinhji-bhavsinhji.summary: Last Maharaja of the princely state of Porbandar, ruling from 1908 until it merged into India in 1948; a member of the Jethwa dynasty, he died in 1979.

thondaman-dynasty.name: Thondaiman dynasty
thondaman-dynasty.summary: A dynasty that ruled the Pudukkottai region in southern India from the 17th to 20th century, founded by Raghunatha Thondaiman.

pudukkottai.name: Pudukkottai
pudukkottai.summary: A city in Tamil Nadu, India, on the Vellar River, historically ruled by the Mutharaiyar dynasty, Cholas, Pandyas and the Thondaimans; today it is a district headquarters with a population of about 118,000.

pudukkottai-kingdom.name: Pudukkottai
pudukkottai-kingdom.summary: A kingdom and later princely state in British India, from 1680 to 1948, covering present-day Pudukkottai district in Tamil Nadu; allied with the British East India Company, it came under Company protection in 1800.

sarvepalli-radhakrishnan.name: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan
sarvepalli-radhakrishnan.summary: Indian philosopher and statesman who served as Vice President (1952–1962) and President of India (1962–1967), reinterpreted Advaita Vedanta for modern readers, and was seen as a bridge between Indian and Western thought.

advaita-vedanta.name: Advaita Vedanta
advaita-vedanta.summary: Hindu philosophical tradition holding that the individual self is ultimately identical with the universal Brahman, and that liberation comes from realizing this oneness.

jadunath-sinha.name: Jadunath Sinha
jadunath-sinha.summary: Indian philosopher, writer and religious seeker who lived from 1892 to 1978.

indian-premier-league.name: Indian Premier League
indian-premier-league.summary: A professional Twenty20 cricket league in India founded in 2007, regarded as the world's most commercially successful cricket league.

twenty20.name: Twenty20
twenty20.summary: Shortened cricket format with each team batting for a maximum of 20 overs, introduced by England's cricket board in 2003 to create a faster, more spectator-friendly game.

zoroastrianism.name: Zoroastrianism
zoroastrianism.summary: An ancient Iranian religion founded on the teachings of Zoroaster, centred on the deity Ahura Mazda and the choice between truth and chaos, once Greater Iran's dominant faith under the Sassanid Empire.

bah-faith.name: Baháʼí Faith
bah-faith.summary: A religion founded by Baháʼu'lláh in 19th-century Iran teaching the unity of all religions and people, with 7 to 8 million followers worldwide today.

rajiv-gandhi.name: Rajiv Gandhi
rajiv-gandhi.summary: Indian prime minister from 1984 to 1989, taking office at age 40 after his mother Indira Gandhi's assassination, and later assassinated himself in 1991.

ek-ladki-ko-dekha-toh-aisa-laga.name: Ek Ladki Ko Dekha Toh Aisa Laga
ek-ladki-ko-dekha-toh-aisa-laga.summary: A 2019 Indian Hindi film about a closeted lesbian woman's attempts to come out to her traditional family, released to positive reviews as a mainstream Bollywood lesbian romance.
ek-ladki-ko-dekha-toh-aisa-laga.source_title: Ek Ladki Ko Dekha Toh Aisa Laga

sonam-kapoor.name: Sonam Kapoor
sonam-kapoor.summary: Indian former actress and fashion icon, born 1985, known for portraying ordinary Indian women on screen and winning a National Film Award and Filmfare Award.

priyakanta-laishram.name: Priyakanta Laishram
priyakanta-laishram.summary: Priyakanta Laishram: An Indian filmmaker from Manipur whose film Oneness was Manipur's first film centered on same-sex relationships.

sarnaism.name: Sarnaism
sarnaism.summary: A nature-worshipping faith of indigenous communities in eastern India's Chota Nagpur Plateau, centered on sacred groves called Sarna and reverence for water, forest and land; India's largest tribal religion.

gondi-people.name: Gondi people
gondi-people.summary: Ethnolinguistic group in India speaking the Dravidian Gondi language, who historically formed kingdoms such as Gondwana and Garha and today number several million.

sari-dharam.name: Sari Dharam
sari-dharam.summary: The traditional religion of the Santal people of eastern India, also practiced in Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan, with the Jomsim Binti as its sacred book.

donyi-polo.name: Donyi-Polo
donyi-polo.summary: A revivalist animist and shamanic movement formalised from the late 1960s among Tani and other Tibeto-Burman peoples of Northeast India, partly in response to the spread of Christianity.

sanamahism.name: Sanamahism
sanamahism.summary: An ethnic, polytheistic religion of the Meitei people of Manipur in northeast India, named after the deity Sanamahi, son of the supreme god and goddess.

buddh-international-circuit.name: Buddh International Circuit
buddh-international-circuit.summary: Indian motor racing circuit in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, opened in 2011 and host of the Formula One Indian Grand Prix that year.

indian-grand-prix.name: Indian Grand Prix
indian-grand-prix.summary: A Formula One race held at the Buddh International Circuit in Uttar Pradesh from 2011 to 2013, first won by Sebastian Vettel.

madurai.name: Madurai
madurai.summary: Major city in Tamil Nadu, India, on the Vaigai River, one of the oldest cities in South Asia with a documented history of more than 2,500 years.
